request.spec:

capital letters not yet a grade; anything else is refused. A new grade appears in every grade
select, the summary, the rates and the rate calendar.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Grades can be added (an entry and a button; GRADE_ADDED grade=<grade>): a code of one to three
capital letters not yet a grade; anything else is refused. A new grade appears in every grade
select, the summary, the rates and the rate calendar.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Grades can now be added, and every check the test makes passes except one line in the spec that no app could pass.

**Test results** (`bin/e2e`): 3 of the 4 tests pass. "grades editable scenario 1" fails at `acceptance.spec.ts:283`, which expects the parent sheet to show the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"`. A few lines earlier the test sets the parent to `${sheet}-p`, so the app correctly shows the real id (e.g. `smvljq9cod0u3-p`). The placeholder was never filled in when the spec was written. To check the rest of that scenario, I ran a temporary copy of the spec with only that line changed to `${sheet}-p`. All 4 tests in the copy passed, audit records included. I then deleted the copy; the real spec is untouched.

**Port:** your environment sets `PORT=3002`, but something outside this sandbox is already listening there. My first run started no server and tested against whatever was on that port. I left that process alone and ran with `PORT=3917 bin/e2e`.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new per-sheet grade table (`V122__sheet_grade.sql`) that also widens every grade column to 3 characters. `V123__grade_checks.java` drops the database checks that only allowed A/B/C; it's a Java migration because H2 auto-named those checks, so plain SQL couldn't drop them. Cloning a sheet now copies its added grades.
- **Server:** a new `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/grades` endpoint. It accepts a trimmed code of 1–3 capital letters that isn't already a grade and writes `GRADE_ADDED sheet=<id> by=<user> grade=<grade>`. A refused add writes nothing. Everywhere grades are checked (people form, inline grade, bulk grade, people import, rates, rate import, retire, merge) now uses the sheet's own list: A, B, C, then added grades in the order added.
- **Front end:** the Grades panel has the code entry (`grade-add-code`) and button (`grade-add`), with refusals shown in `grade-error`. New grades appear in every grade select, the summary, the current rates, the rate calendar, the rate preview, the consolidated figures and the other-sheet compare.

The per-grade settings (`terms-X`, `grace-X` and the like) and the default-grade setting still accept only A, B and C. The request didn't cover them, but say if you want those extended too.
